title: Thinking LLMs: General Instruction Following with Thought Generation
summary: The optional pairwise ELO MLE can be undefined under allowed unanimous rankings. This is a Minor specification defect in an auxiliary, interchangeable pairwise-to-scalar scoring procedure; the common TPO objective does not require this unregularized estimator. The historical STE solver and preference-selection effect remain Needs Evidence.
limitations: No author code or raw evaluation outputs available/executed.
No uncertainty estimates reconstructed from weighted verdicts.
Character counts do not verify FLOPs or wall-clock cost.
Qualitative examples not fully independently audited.

problems.title: Unregularized pairwise ELO scores may not exist

source_claim.paraphrase: Determine finite scalar scores by maximizing the printed logistic battle likelihood.

assumptions: Two presentation orders per candidate pair
Both orders agree on a strict total ordering
K8 as in setup; no ties or parse errors
No unreported regularizer, bound, artificial comparison or stopping fallback
problems.check: For K2, B12=2,B21=0 yields 2log(sigmoid(d)), strictly increasing to unattained0. For K8, centered scores proportional to(3.5,2.5,...,-3.5) likewise send all winning margins to infinity, objective to0 with no finite maximum.
problems.result: The estimator is not defined for an allowed comparison outcome.
counterevidence: Practical finite optimizer/regularizer may resolve it but was not available.
Pure best/worst ranking can be obvious despite divergent scores.
Default ArmoRM scores and headline results do not use this estimator.
problems.core_dependency: The common TPO objective and response-based preference-pair construction accept scalar scores without requiring this particular unregularized ELO estimator. The defect lies in an auxiliary, interchangeable conversion used by the optional STE branch; length-controlled selection there can depend on the numerical fallback.
problems.impact: Minor specification defect on this dependency basis. The existence counterexample is demonstrated; the historical STE fallback and its effect on length-controlled preference selection remain Needs Evidence.

correction.statement: Specify a penalized or bounded estimator and hyperparameters. Positive L2 penalty makes objective strictly concave/coercive, giving finite unique solution.
